wings.description: The technocrats around Baran himself are credible abroad and disliked at home. They want the stabilisation programme and believe competence will eventually become a constituency.
wings.name: The Circle

wings.description: Diaspora money and diaspora certainty: hardest on the Union, softest on the market, and impatient for the country they remember to be restored in stone as well as policy.
wings.name: The Return

wings.description: Vashtera lawyers, importers and the new banks, interested in government chiefly as a source of licences.
wings.name: The Capital Bar

wings.description: Kestrel Square veterans who are genuinely democratic and genuinely nationalist. They regard the republic as the achievement for which their dead friends paid.
wings.name: The Square

wings.description: Irredentists with army connections, for whom Vetrenka is the only issue and Doncic's silence is a standing invitation.
wings.name: The Line

wings.description: Anera and the Church: the current that would have to decide what to do if Dorin Vasca ever walked back into public life.
wings.name: The Parish

wings.description: The Zavost union machine delivers the party's votes and expects the party to protect the plants in return.
wings.name: The Works

wings.description: Former ministry cadres who know how the state functions and are among the few people in the Chamber capable of administering it. A breach with the Works would cost the government its majority.
wings.name: The Reform Wing

wings.description: Those who received land when the collectives dissolved. They will trade on questions outside land, credit and diesel, and do not pretend otherwise.
wings.name: The Grange

wings.description: Those who did not receive land in the dissolution, angrier than the Grange and available to whoever promises a second settlement.
wings.name: The Left-Out

wings.description: Genuine industrial militancy with the organisational reach to call a general strike in Zavost.
wings.name: The Shop Floor

wings.description: The residue of the Dravist old guard: four seats shared with the Shop Floor, and a memory of a state that paid wages.
wings.name: The Nostalgics

event_history: [1 Mar 1993] Prime Minister Maren Steele takes office this month leading the Liberal Democrats with Social Democrats, after the Reckoning — the first government since the Turn of the Year that anyone actually voted for.

[1 Mar 1993] Maren Steele's political inheritance: Cyrus Baran's project, and the closest thing the transition has to an establishment: reform-minded Union-era technocrats, diaspora returnees and Awakening moderates who never trusted Vasca. Market reform, integration westward, and a civic rather than ethnic idea of who counts as Ardenian.

[1 Mar 1993] The national inheritance is shared by government and opposition alike: an economy still bleeding from the Union's collapse and a ceasefire line through Vetrenka that nobody in the chamber recognises.

milestones: Prime Minister Maren Steele takes office in Ardenia (normal difficulty).

active_laws.name: Fiscal Consolidation Act
